subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by making routine CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with no-maintenance read-only fallbacks, or by adding a stronger gateway-owned single-writer lease for shared state DB access?
rationale: Both approaches can address the reported data-loss class, but they have different compatibility impact for diagnostics, doctor migrations, recovery, and operator workflows while the gateway is running.

options.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make routine health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and only allow direct file reads that disable WAL maintenance and migrations while the gateway owns the DB.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: Have the gateway hold an explicit state DB ownership lease and make all other writer or maintenance-capable opens fail closed or route through the gateway.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation direction until the sanitized bundle or native better-sqlite3 stress harness proves the specific corrupting interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make routine health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and only allow direct file reads that disable WAL maintenance and migrations while the gateway owns the DB.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest shared-state history signal and the issue discussion names the product decision as needing their direction.
